item.title: Bar complaint filed against DOJ lawyer over warrant for reporter’s home
item.description: A complaint urges Virginia State Bar to discipline DOJ lawyer Gordon D. Kromberg for allegedly withholding legal info in a warrant for a Washington Post reporter.

item.title: St. Cloud immigration lawyer helps clients navigate 2026 uncertainty
item.description: Stacey Rogers, a St. Cloud immigration lawyer, guides clients through 2026 visa delays and enforcement concerns with clear legal advice and emotional support.

item.title: Olympic curler Ruohonen denounces ICE sweeps
item.description: Curler and attorney Rich Ruohonen spoke out against immigration sweeps in Minnesota during the 2026 Winter Olympics, highlighting constitutional rights and community values.

item.title: Trump-appointed judge blocks DOJ request for Michigan voter list
item.description: A Trump-appointed judge rejected the DOJ's request for Michigan's full voter list, citing privacy concerns over sensitive voter information.

item.title: Grand jury declines to indict six Democratic lawmakers
item.description: A D.C. grand jury declined to indict six Democratic lawmakers investigated for comments advising military members to reject illegal orders.

item.title: DOJ requests examples of judges blocking agenda for congressional review
item.description: The Justice Department asked U.S. attorneys for examples of judges allegedly obstructing its agenda to aid Congress in potential impeachment actions.

item.title: 8th Circuit upholds Minnesota COVID testing policy
item.description: The 8th Circuit Court upheld Minnesota's weekly COVID-19 testing policy for unvaccinated state employees under the ADA, citing business necessity and job-related safety.

item.title: Trump’s repeal of climate rule opens a ‘new front’ for litigation
item.description: The EPA's repeal of the 2009 greenhouse gas endangerment finding could lead to increased public nuisance lawsuits against power companies and industries.

item.title: Court of Appeals judge reprimanded after DWI
item.description: Minnesota Court of Appeals Judge Renee Worke was publicly reprimanded after pleading guilty to misdemeanor driving while impaired in 2025.

item.title: Walz appoints Susan DeVos to 5th District bench
item.description: Susan DeVos has been appointed by Gov. Tim Walz as a district court judge in Minnesota’s 5th Judicial District, serving Blue Earth County and surrounding areas.
